sentences.text: The brief facts of the case is that the land bearing Sy.No. 62/1A-1 measuring 2 acres 32 guntas of Konena Agrahara, Vartur Hobli, Bengaluru South Taluka has been acquired in-favour of Airports Authority.
Preliminary notification was issued on 17.12.1994.
Final notification was issued on 18.01.1995.
The L.A.O. has passed the award on 15.05.1996 fixing market value at Rs. 6,20,000/- per acre.
The claimant not satisfied with the award had filed objections before the L.A.O..
As the L.A.O. has failed to send the reference, the claimant filed L.A.C. No. 243/2002.
This Court by order dated 01.04.2003 has allowed the said petition and L.A.C. No. 13/2004 had directed the respondent to send the reference.
In pursuance to the said direction, the L.A.O. has sent the reference.
.3. On receipt of the reference, Court notice has issued to the claimant.
In response to which, the claimant appeared through its advocate and filed claim statement.

.4. The claimant has stated that a sum of Rs.40,64,00,000/- claimed by it represents the fair market value of the subject land on the date of the preliminary notification; the award has not taken into consideration the potential of the subject land, the purpose for which it could be employed, the value of the properties surrounding the subject land, the state development of the subject land and its surroundings, the loss that has occasioned to the applicant from severance of the subject land from its abutting property survey numbers and other factors contemplated under Section 23 of the Act.

It is stated that the award is arbitrary and is not based in justifiable material; the applicant had no opportunity to substantiate its claim for compensation; measurement of the subject land has been incorrectly mentioned as against the correct extent of 2 acres 36 guntas.
Hence, prayed for enhancement of compensation.

The respondent No. 2 has filed objections stating that the reference sought for by the petitioner before the Special Land Acquisition Officer was subsequent to the period contemplated under the Provisions of Section 18(2) of the Land Acquisition Act 1894, (Karnataka Amendment) and as such on this ground alone the reference would have to be rejected.

It is submitted that the reference itself is not maintainable in law in view of the fact that the petitioner was not a person entitled under law to hold, own possess the land in question either during the Acquisition Proceedings or during the Proceedings of the Award, as the nature of the land in question was an agricultural land; in view of the specific bar under the Provisions of the Karnataka Land Reforms Act for any non agriculturist, more particularly a Company from holding agricultural land, in the absence of any material to substantiate that the petitioner was legally entitled to hold and own the land in question, the Reference/ Claim is unsustainable.
.6. The second respondent further submits that the above petition is barred by limitation.
The claim of Rs. 40,64,00,000/- is exorbitant, unconscionable, without any basis and without any reasonable calculation.
The reference itself is not maintainable for L.A.C. No. 13/2004 the grounds stated in the Preliminary Objections herein above and on merits.
.7. In order to substantiate the case, the Managing Director of claimant has been examined as PW.1 and has got marked documents as Ex.P.1 and 2(a).

The General Manager of the respondent No.2 has M/S. Blaze And Central Pvt. Ltd vs The Slao on 13 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/78329822/
2 been examined as RW.1.
.8.

The respondent No. 2 has filed written arguments.

The counsel for the respondent No. 2 has filed the following decisions, they are:

The said decisions are taken on note.

.9. The points that would arise for my consideration are:
1. Whether the reference is in time?
L.A.C. No. 13/2004 2. Whether the compensation awarded by the L.A.O., to the claimant is in-adequate?
3. What Order or Award?
.10. My findings on the above points are as follows:-
Point No.1 :

In the affirmative,
 Point No.2 : Partly in the affirmative,
 Point No.3 :

As per the final order for the following:-
 R E A SON S .11.
Point No.1:- The respondent has taken up contention that the reference is beyond period of limitation contemplated under Section 18 of the said Act.
As the respondent had not sent the reference, the claimant had filed L.A.C. No. 243/2002 under Section 18(3)(b) of L.A. Act, to send the reference.
The said petition is allowed on 01.04.2003.
The learned Judge considered the aspect as to whether the application under Section 18(3)(b) is in time.
The learned judge has answered the point in affirmative.
The said order has attained finality, this Court cannot once-again examine as to whether the reference sent is in time.
Hence, point No. 1 for consideration is answered in affirmative.
L.A.C. No. 13/2004 .12. Point No.2:

The claimant is seeking enhanced compensation, in this reference, contending that the market value of his acquired land, as on the date of publication of 4(1)
notification was much more higher than the market value fixed by the L.A.O., under the circumstances, the burden is on the claimant to prove that the market value fixed by the L.A.O., to his acquired land and compensation paid to him, is meager and inadequate.

The well known methods of determining the market value of the acquired land are expert's opinion, sales statistics M/S. Blaze And Central Pvt. Ltd vs The Slao on 13 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/78329822/
3 method, yield (income) method, sale of comparable lands or judgment of court, in-respect of the comparable lands.

sentences.text: .13. The Managing Director Lalit M. Bijlani has been examined as PW.1 and has filed the affidavit in support of his plea in this reference with regard to the acquisition of 2 acres 32 guntas of land in Sy.No. 52/1A-1, situated at Konena Agrahara , Vartur Hobli for extension of airport.

He has stated that the acquired land is very near to Vidhana Soudha, Railway station and Shivajinagara and City market etc.; the acquired property is adjoining and abutting to the HAL Airport authorities and situated facing towards the main road.

The purpose of acquisition of property itself is for L.A.C. No.
13/2004 commercial one.

He has stated that the HAL and Airport road, on which the acquired property is situated, is one of the most prominent and important business road, in the entire city of Bengaluru; HAL road was long back developed and so many commercial establishments were already developed and some of the nationalized banks are also established near the property was acquired; the potential value of the land situated on the HAL road, is virtually was that of M.G. road and other important roads in the vicinity.
He has stated that the acquired property is situated on HAL road and easily termed as one of the most expensive piece of real estate in the City of Bengaluru.

.14. PW.1 has stated that if the large extent of land is available in high profile road such as HAL road,
the value of such land will be nearly thrice the value of smaller extent of land in the same area.

PW.1 has stated that the acquisition purpose itself clearly goes to show and establishes that the property is situated in a highly commercial area and the L.A.O. acquired the land for commercial purpose only i.e., for Internal Terminal Project.

The extra value that such a large properties fetch is due to the fact that if the extent of land is large, huge commercial complexes consisting L.A.C. No. 13/2004 of 8 to 10 floors can be constructed as compared to only 2 or 3 storied buildings.
PW.1 has stated that the value of the property has got more potential value and he failed to consider the same.

He has stated that having regard to the size of the land and with regard to the fact that the acquired property is situated in HAL road, it would be fair and reasonable to determine and fix the market value at least Rs. 4,000/- per sq. feet.

He has stated that value of the acquired property determined by the L.A.O.
is very meager.

The sale deeds considered by the L.A.O. were in-respect of period of 2 years prior to the notification; that the entire procedure adopted by the L.A.O. in assessing the market value is improper, irrational and wholly incorrect.

.15. PW.1 has stated that he has purchased the acquired property for commercial purposes and further said acquired property if formerly mentioned as Survey Numbers, it has lost its agricultural character long back and it is absolutely commercial in nature since it is situated on the main road and abutting to the H.A.L Airport Authority.

The acquired property is situated at the time of acquisition and the property is situated within the limits of BBMP and it has lost its agricultural character L.A.O., ought to L.A.C. No. 13/2004 have awarded compensation on square feet only.

He has stated that fixation of the market value for collecting stamp duty reflects, the true market value of the property being sold and purchased, and its therefore submitted that in the respect of the land acquired the Court be pleased to determine the market value at Rs.4,000/- per square ft. (1994) 4 SCC 595.
The Hon'ble Supreme Court has held register maintained by Registering Authority for collection of Stamp duty has no statutory foundation to determine market value.

To substantiate M/S. Blaze And Central Pvt. Ltd vs The Slao on 13 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/78329822/
4 that the market value of Rs. 4,000/- per square ft.

sentences.text: Claimant has not produced guidelines issued by the Government for fixation of market value for collecting stamp duty for the relevant period.
.16. PW.1 has stated that another means of determining of the market value would be the annual rental income that the developed property fetches.

If the rental income is taken into consideration for fixing fair market value of the acquired property, the market value would be at-least 4,000/- per square ft. as property is being acquired for the purpose of parking value on the rental basis.
To substantiate the same claimant has not stated how he as arrived at the calculation.

PW.1 has stated that, that acquired property is about 1,26,324 per Sq.ft and the property is abutting to HAL Airport Authority and commercial in nature and any builders would have easily to develop the property by constructing multistoried building, wherein he can easily entitled to sell 50% of the said buildup area and he would have earned easily a huge sum of Rupees Forty crores without investing any money at all.
The claimant has not produced any agreement in this regard.
In the absence of exemplar deed the same cannot be considered.
.18. The claimant has relied upon Ex.P.1 and Ex.P.1 judgment in MFA No.6781/2006.

On perusal of the judgment it is seen that 24 guntas of land in Survey No.46/2b of Devarabisanahalli Village was acquired by the Government for the purpose of implementation of the scheme of formation of outer ring road between Varthur Road and Sarjapura Road, in pursuance of preliminary notification dated 06.04.1992 issued by the BDA.
L.A.O. has determined the compensation at Rs.3,30,000/- per acre.
The reference Court has enhanced to the compensation to Rs.100/- per Sq. foot,.
The Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has modified the judgment and award and has determined that market value at L.A.C. No. 13/2004 Rs.75/- per Sq. foot.
The claimant has stated that the property in the said case is situated 10 Kms away from his property and acquired property is to be awarded on the basis of Square feet only.

.19. The claimant has relied upon the judgment in MFA No.2020/2001 (Ex.P.2) and connected cases wherein The Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has confirmed the order passed by the reference Court fixing market value at Rs. 100/- per Sq. foot in respect of acquired survey number.
On perusal of the said judgment it does not disclose the date of preliminary notification.
So this judgment can not be relied to fix the market value in this case.
PW.1 has been cross examined.
Nothing substantial has been elicited.
.20. The General Manager of the Airports Authority has been examined as RW.1.
He has stated that the reference is not maintainable.
In view of the fact that the petitioner was not a person entitled under law to hold, own and possess.

In view of the provisions of the Karnataka Land Reforms Act,
for any non agriculturist, more particularly a company from holding agricultural land.
It is stated that in the absence of any material to substantiate that the petitioner was entitled to hold and own the L.A.C. No. 13/2004 land, claim is not sustainable.
The claimant has already received the compensation.
So, the respondent cannot raise this objection in this reference.

.21. RW.1 has stated that, L.A.O. has taken into account all the aspects in the acquisition proceedings and the said land was agricultural land and even the petitioner has claimed it only as a agricultural M/S.

sentences.text: land: that the petitioner is attempting to exaggerate the claim by imposing these reasons for enhancement and the same is not justified.
RW.1 has stated that, respondent No.1 has followed that procedure in fixing market value; the claim of the Rs, 40,64,00,000/- is exorbitant.
Hence, prays for dismissal.
.22. The claimant has not cross examined the witness.
The respondent No.1 has not been examined.
The award discloses that L.A.O. has called for sales statistics for the period of 3 years prior to notification and has arrived at a figure of Rs.6,20,211/- per acre.
The award also discloses that the acquired property is very near to Bengaluru Airports.

LAO has relied upon sale deed in respect of Sy No.52/1A, measuring 2 acres 36 guntas sold by KB Venkatareddy to be claimant at Rs.2,89,224/-
per acre in the year 1986.

He has added appreciation at 15% and has arrived at a figure of Rs.
L.A.C. No. 13/2004 5,50,000/-.
The L.A.O. has fixed the compensation of Rs. 6,20,000/- per acre.

.23. The appreciation of oral evidence of PW.1 and documentary evidence, it is evident that claimant in the instant case has not adduced and got marked the sale deeds of the surrounding lands which were executed 3 years prior to the preliminary notification u/s. 4(1) of L.A. Act, as such, it is evident that there is no scope for this court to resort to the Sales Statistics method to arrive at market value of the acquired land in this case.
.24. From the evidence of PW.1 and award, it is clear that the land acquired is adjacent to the airports.
Though the property was an agricultural land, it has more potential value for non agricultural use, in view of the geographical location and the property being surrounded by well developed place.

.25. A perusal of oral evidence of PW.1 leads leads to the only probability that the acquired land covered under Ex.P.1 judgment which is 10 kms further away from the acquired land of Konena Agrahara, covered in this reference.
As such, the acquired property has more potentiality.
Now law is well settled that the decided judgment of any of the reference Court can be relied upon in order to come to just and fair conclusion in-respect of fixing just and fair compensation.

In this regard, I would like to bank upon the following decisions reported in AIR 2003 Supreme Court 4382 wherein it is held as under:
" (A) Land Acquisition Act (1 of 1894), S2- Compensation-Determination of, on basis of earlier judgments-Plea that High Court erred in not taking sale instances into account while fixing compensation- Compensation already fixed by High Court in earlier proceedings and Supreme Court in one such proceeding has already approved rate fixed-Best method would be to look at the earlier judgments and Awards and not sale instances - High Court cannot be faulted for having fixed compensation on the basis of earlier judgments" & one more decision which came to be reported in 2005(4) KCCR short notes 264 (General Manager, ONGC V/s Sendhabal Vastram Patel & others), which is as M/S. 6 under:
L.A.C. No. 13/2004 " Land Acquisition Act, 1894, Section 18 - market value - the best method for determining market value of acquired land is the amount which a willing purchaser of the land would pay to the owner of the land as may be evidenced by deeds of sale

- in the absence of any direct evidence on the said point, the Court may take recourse to other methods, viz., judgments and awards passed in-respect of acquisitions of lands made in the same village and/or neighbouring villages.

The Reference Court has to apply the comparable sales method and also the situation of the land, which is to be appreciated upon considering the question as to whether acquired land is similar to any land sold in the vicinity".
.27.
So far as Ex.P.1 M.F.A. No. 6781/2006 is concerned, land in Ex.P.1 is situated in Devarabeesanahalli, Vartur Hobli, whereas the land in the present case is situated in the same Hobli.
Ex.P.1 judgment can be relied for fixing market value in the present case.

As per Ex.P.1 judgment the Hon'ble High Court has L.A.C. No. 13/2004 determined the market value at Rs.75/-
per sq. foot.
In the present case, though the land is an agricultural land it has all potential of non agricultural purpose.
The compensation can be determined on the basis of square foot.
The land acquired in Ex.P.1 under preliminary notification dated 06.04.1992, whereas, the land in the present case is on 17.12.1994.
There is difference of 2 years 8 months between two notifications.

.28. The learned counsel for the respondent has produced a decision reported in (2004) 2 SCC 283 wherein the Hon'ble Supreme Court has held that:
" Market value of the land - Appreciation in - Held on facts, appreciation at the rate of 15% for every subsequent year reasonable"
.29.
In the present case the land is situated adjacent to the Airport.
The L.A.O. has calculated the appreciation at the rate of 15% on the sale deed relied by him.
In view of the above decision, I am of the view that 15% appreciation can be given for difference in the notifications.
Hence, the market value in the present case is fixed at Rs. 75 X 15% X 2 years 8 months = Rs. 105/- per sq. foot.
PW.1 has stated that there are nearly 50 coconut trees in the property.

The L.A.O. without considering the age of the trees has awarded a very meager compensation of Rs.
41,250/-.
He has stated that taking into consideration, the yield of the said coconut trees, which are 10 years in age the L.A.O. ought to have awarded a minimum compensation of Rs. 5,00,000/-.
The award discloses that there were 30 coconut trees in the acquired property.
The claimant has not produced the yield certificate nor any materials to show that the coconut trees were 10 years old.
In the absence of documents, the claim of the claimant is rejected.
The compensation awarded by the L.A.O. is accepted with regard to the malkies.

.31. The appreciation of oral and documentary evidence, on record, leads to the unmistakable fact that the claimant proves that the market value fixed by the respondent - L.A.O., in-respect of his acquired land, in this case, is unjust, inadequate and on lower side.

Thus, the claimant in this case, is M/S. Blaze And Central Pvt. Ltd vs The Slao on 13 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/78329822/
7 entitle for enhanced market value at Rs.105/- per sq. foot, instead of Rs.6,20,000/- per acre,
awarded by the L.A.O., for his acquired land, with all statutory benefits.

sentences.text: The claimant is entitle for the aforesaid market L.A.C. No. 13/2004 value of his acquired land and consequently the statutory benefits from the date of publication of preliminary notification.
Hence, I answer point No.2 partly in the Affirmative.
.32. Point No.3:-

In view of my findings on the afore- mentioned points 1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:-
OR D E R
The reference made by the Land Acquisition Officer/ respondent No.1 under Section 18 of L.A. Act, 1894 is partly allowed.
The market value of the acquired property bearing Sy.No. 62/1A-1 measuring 2 acres 32 guntas, situated at Konana Agrahara, Vartur Hobli, Bengaluru South Taluka, is fixed at Rs.105/- per sq. foot.

Claimant is entitled for enhanced market value of Rs.105/- per sq. foot instead of Rs.
6,20,000/- per acre, on production of document for having received compensation from LAO/Court.
The amount already paid by LAO has to be deducted.

L.A.C. No. 13/2004 Claimant is entitled for additional market value under Section 23(1-A) of L.A. Act, at the rate of 12% p.a., on the enhanced market value from the date of publication of Preliminary notification till date of passing award.
Claimant is entitled for solatium at the rate of 30% on the enhanced market value as per Section 23(2) of L.A. Act.

Claimant is entitled for interest at the rate of 9% p.a.,
on the enhanced market value, solatium and additional market value for a period of one year from the date of taking possession of acquired land and further interest at the rate of 15% p.a., for subsequent years, till deposit of entire compensation amount.
The advocate fee is fixed at  Rs.1,000/-.
Draw Award Accordingly.

In the present case, though the land is an agricultural land it has all potential of non agricultural purpose.
The compensation can be determined on the basis of square foot.
The land acquired in Ex.P.1 under preliminary notification dated 06.04.1992, whereas, the land in the present case is on 17.12.1994.
There is difference of 2 years 8 months between two notifications.
The award discloses that there were 30 coconut trees in the acquired property.
The claimant has not produced the yield certificate nor any materials to show that the coconut trees were 10 years old.

In view of my findings on the afore- mentioned points 1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:-
OR D E R
The reference made by the Land Acquisition Officer/ respondent No.1 under Section 18 of L.A. Act, 1894 is partly allowed.
The market value of the acquired property bearing Sy.No. 62/1A-1 measuring 2 acres 32 guntas, situated at Konana Agrahara, Vartur Hobli, Bengaluru South Taluka, is fixed at Rs.105/- per sq. foot.
Claimant is entitled for enhanced market value of Rs.105/- per sq. foot instead of Rs.
6,20,000/- per acre, on production of document for having received compensation from LAO/Court.
The amount already paid by LAO has to be deducted.
L.A.C. No. 13/2004 Claimant is entitled for additional market value under Section 23(1-A) of L.A. Act, at the rate of 12% p.a., on the enhanced market value from the date of publication of Preliminary notification till date of passing award.
Claimant is entitled for solatium at the rate of 30% on the enhanced market value as per Section 23(2) of L.A. Act.
Claimant is entitled for interest at the rate of 9% p.a.,
on the enhanced market value, solatium and additional market value for a period of one year from the date of taking possession of acquired land and further interest at the rate of 15% p.a., for subsequent years, till deposit of entire compensation amount.
The advocate fee is fixed at  Rs.1,000/-.
Draw Award Accordingly.
